page: Amazon Web Services g6.2xlarge is an accelerated computing instance built on the AWS Nitro System, designed for machine learning inference and graphics-intensive tasks. The system is powered by an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor clocked at 3.4 GHz, supplying 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU cache architecture provides 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache, backed by 32 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio.

Hardware acceleration is delivered by a single NVIDIA L4 GPU featuring 22 GB of video memory based on the Ada Lovelace architecture. In benchmark evaluations, this configuration demonstrates top-tier throughput in prompt processing and text generation for small (135M) and medium (7B) large language model workloads. Local ephemeral storage includes a bundled 450 GB NVMe solid-state drive, accompanied by a 5 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile.

Benchmark testing indicates strong single-core CPU execution alongside average multi-core and general computational performance across Geekbench and PassMark suites. Large-block uncached system memory bandwidth is a notable architectural constraint, measuring in the lower performance tier. However, the consolidation of dedicated GPU acceleration, balanced CPU resources, and onboard NVMe storage provides a cost-efficient hardware profile for deploying real-time AI inference services, video processing, and graphics virtualization workloads without provisioning standalone high-tier training clusters.
description: Amazon Web Services g6.2xlarge is an accelerated computing instance tailored for machine learning inference and graphics processing. Powered by the Nitro hypervisor, it features an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor providing 8 dedicated vCPUs, 32 GB of DDR4 system memory, and a 5 Gbps baseline network capacity. Hardware acceleration is supplied by an onboard NVIDIA L4 GPU with 22 GB of VRAM, complemented by a bundled 450 GB local NVMe SSD. In benchmark evaluations, the instance records top-tier throughput in small and medium parameter language model inference, backed by strong single-core CPU results. While uncached large-block host memory bandwidth reflects a relative bottleneck, the instance maintains balanced host memory allocation and low-latency local storage. This profile delivers high resource efficiency for deployment scenarios such as real-time LLM inference, video encoding, computer vision pipelines, and interactive graphics rendering.
